data.gender_notes: Jayavathi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jayavathi is a name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Jaya', which means victory, and 'Vathi', which means goddess. The name is often associated with the goddess Durga and signifies the triumph of good over evil. The name Jayavathi carries the meaning “Victorious Goddess” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jayavathi usually hope their child will grow to embody victorious goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Emblem of victory over inner demons and outer obstacles

vedic_reference.note: Jayavathi is not a name mentioned in the Vedas or any other Indian scriptures, but it is derived from the Sanskrit language and the meaning of victory is widely used in Hinduism.

historical_references.reference: Jayavathi was the name of the queen consort of King Vijayaditya of the Chalukya dynasty of Karnataka, South India. She was renowned for her beauty and is remembered in Indian literature for her role in the love story between her and the poet-saint, Basava.

Jayavathi was also the name of the wife of King Bhillama II of the Yadava dynasty of the Deccan Plateau in present-day Maharashtra, India. She is famously known for her role in the conflict between her husband and the Chalukyas, where she is said to have played a decisive role in the Battle of Kalyani in 1192 CE, helping her husband win the battle and establish his kingdom.

One popular instance is the Telugu movie 'Jayavathi', where the protagonist is named after the ancient river goddess. The name is also commonly used as a hashtag on Instagram for posts related to South Indian traditions and culture. On Reddit, there are several communities and discussions dedicated to Jayavathi and other river goddesses from Indian mythology.
